gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Big, loud, and scattered wide. Paprika sets lowercase that fills the line like capitals, while Noto Sans Nabataean, a sans-serif with near cap-tall lowercase, follows below. Its open s curves keep paragraphs moving.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-nag-mundari: Paprika's lowercase fills the line like capitals, with counters that breathe like a hollow reed cut open. Noto Sans Nag Mundari follows as a plain sans whose half-unwrapped c and s shapes keep the text lively beneath it.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-nandinagari: Noto Sans Nandinagari reads friendly and generous, its short ascenders and big lowercase body leaving openings wide at every weight. Give it a little more size than feels necessary beside Paprika.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Loud letters, set far apart. Noto Sans Nushu rises with a towering x-height and terminals held far from the stroke body, so Paprika's commanding display forms get a modern, tall-bodied sans-serif to push against.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Paprika spaces its letters far apart and lets lowercase fill the line like capitals, which gives headings real muscle. Noto Sans Ogham brings wide gaps in the e, so a slightly smaller size still feels sturdy.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Paprika arrives loud, with scattered letters. Noto Sans Ol Chiki is a sans-serif whose curve tails sit well back from the body, so words read as solid blocks rather than skylines under that expressive heading.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-old-hungaria: Paprika's lowercase fills the line like capitals, with counters that breathe like a hollow reed cut open. Noto Sans Old Hungarian is the quiet worker, its tall a, e and s keeping apertures open even at tiny sizes.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-old-italic: Noto Sans Old Italic reads dense and contemporary, with almost no gap between x-height and cap height. Paprika is the one to make noise with its scattered letters, while this sans-serif keeps curve endings apart for steady reading.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-old-north-ar: Noto Sans Old North Arabian packs a dense, tall lowercase band, its terminals pointing outward like a pair of tongs. Paprika does the shouting with scattered, capital-sized lowercase, and Noto Sans Old North Arabian does the plain sans talking.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-old-permic: Commanding is how Paprika comes across, with letters scattered at a distance and counters like a hollow reed cut open. Noto Sans Old Permic sits beneath as a plain sans, rounded and open, with lowercase nearly matching capitals.
